fact: South Sudan's ICT minister visited the African Telecommunications Union headquarters in Nairobi and pledged deeper collaboration on digital infrastructure, capacity building and standardisation; ATU welcomed it as collaboration among its member states (a visit and pledge, no agreement signed).

The EACO statistics report lists South Sudan as one of the seven member states of the East African Communications Organisation, with its regulator NCA submitting 2024-2025 data (EACO working group 1 coordinates the report).

The Minister of Information, ICT and Postal Services signed a declaration of trust with the Smart Africa alliance to cooperate on the digital economy, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, in a ceremony reported by the ministry on 2025-05-30.

South Sudan, with Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda, took part in the Northern Corridor Integration Projects implementation clusters meeting in Kampala, where the partner states' joint account for a communications satellite feasibility study and the NCIP single digital market programme were discussed; the source gives no meeting date, so the report date is used.
